source_user: A team wants lower serving cost through weight-only quantization. Define a fair comparison. Scenario variant 8: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: fix model and prompts; compare quality, memory, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, concurrency, kernel support, calibration set, and failure cases; report confidence intervals.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions (variant 8): compare the same model revision, tokenizer, serving engine, hardware, topology, software build, request mix, batching policy, concurrency levels, power/thermal policy, and stopping rules. Weight-only quantization must be isolated: record bit width, group size, scale/zero-point scheme, calibration data and outlier handling, and state whether activations or KV cache precision changed. Use an authorized disposable benchmark, redact sensitive prompts and telemetry, and label facts as measured, estimated, or unknown.

Hypothesis and falsification: the candidate quantization lowers cost per successful output token without unacceptable quality, safety, functional, or SLO regression. Predeclare quality and TTFT/TPOT/throughput tolerances and a cost model. Falsify the hypothesis if paired quality or safety tests breach a gate, tail latency or error/retry rates breach an SLO, kernel support causes functional failures, or cost per successful token does not improve after including calibration, memory, throughput, and operational overhead. Competing explanations include dequantization overhead, calibration-set mismatch, memory-bandwidth saturation, batching differences, thermal throttling, and changed failure behavior.

Controlled experiment and measurements: freeze and version the model, prompts, seeds where meaningful, input/output lengths, sampling, scheduler, warmup, and concurrency sweep. Run baseline and quantized variants in randomized paired order with repeated trials and identical placement. Verify output validity and safety, then measure task-quality scores with confidence intervals, peak/resident GPU memory and fragmentation, TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end P50/P95/P99 latency, successful tokens/s, request throughput, queueing, GPU utilization, power, errors, OOMs, retries, and kernel/fallback selection. Use the same calibration split for tuning only and a held-out evaluation split for judging; report denominators and uncertainty, not just averages. Check low-concurrency and saturation regimes separately.

Confounders and rollback: control driver/kernel/library versions, clocks, thermal state, prompt-length distribution, cache state, admission control, and background load; inspect whether a fallback kernel or altered KV cache invalidates the comparison. Preserve raw redacted traces and configuration hashes. Stop the canary and restore the known-good baseline if any safety/functional gate, OOM increase, or predeclared quality/SLO threshold fails; do not claim production savings until repeated paired results and cost assumptions are reviewed.
risks: quality and latency gains may be offset by unsupported or fallback kernels
calibration-set mismatch can hide regressions on production-like prompts
benchmark telemetry or prompts may contain sensitive data
canary rollback may be incomplete if quantized artifacts or routing state persist
evidence_required: versioned model, quantization, calibration, kernel, and serving configurations
paired held-out quality and safety results with confidence intervals
request-level latency, throughput, memory, error, retry, and fallback-kernel traces across concurrency
cost model including calibration, capacity, power, and operational overhead
